result.title: Seeing Through Preferences: Recovering Hidden Local Preference Neighborhoods for Text-to-Image Alignment
result.summary: Aligning text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models with human preferences typically relies on large-scale pairwise annotations, which are expensive to obtain and provide only sparse supervision. Moreover, not all preference comparisons contribute equally to learning: comparisons between semantically distant images often reveal little about the fine-grained perceptual factors underlying human judgments. We argue that informative supervision can arise from local preference neighborhoods surrounding human-preferred images, where semantically aligned alternatives expose meaningful perceptual and structural differences. Motivated by this observation, we propose PrefLens, a framework that recovers local preference neighborhoods from sparse human feedback. Specifically, PrefLens generates controlled perceptual variations around preferred images that largely retain semantic identity and selects compact sets of informative neighbors in a reward-defined preference space induced by pretrained reward models. By transforming each human preference annotation into a structured neighborhood of informative comparisons, PrefLens enriches supervision without requiring additional human labeling. Our experiments and diagnostic evaluations show that the recovered neighborhoods capture human-relevant preference characteristics and provide effective supervision for preference alignment across diverse settings.

AI.brief_summary: 针对文生图偏好对齐中成对标注稀疏的问题，提出 PrefLens，在预训练奖励模型定义的偏好空间里围绕人类偏好图像生成受控感知变体，并筛选紧凑的高信息邻居集，把单条偏好标注扩成结构化比较邻域以增强监督。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「围绕偏好样本构造细粒度对比并筛选高信息邻居」的做法可能为 LVR 中的轨迹/潜在状态监督构造与视觉证据筛选提供可核查的数据侧线索，但本身不涉及多模态推理状态。
